posts.title: The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate
posts.summary:
Is it better to cram more compute into each rack or rethink the architecture?
The post The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Data center operators are preparing for 1-megawatt racks to support the massive power and cooling demands of next-generation AI compute clusters.
Hyperscalers including Google, Meta, and Microsoft are collaborating via the OCP 'Mount Diablo' project to standardize rack infrastructure, cooling, and power delivery.
The shift necessitates moving away from passive rack enclosures toward integrated compute systems that tightly couple liquid cooling, power shelves, and high-speed interconnects.

posts.title: Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip
posts.summary:
As AI clusters push beyond rack-scale limits, optical interconnects and circuit switching are reshaping how data centers scale. 
The post Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Copper interconnects are reaching physical limits regarding signal loss and power consumption, forcing a transition to optical interconnects even within rack-scale environments.
The industry is redefining scaling terminology to include 'scale-in,' which refers to the bandwidth capacity managed within a single chassis.
Optical circuit switching (OCS) is gaining traction as a way to reduce latency and improve GPU utilization, which currently suffers when processors wait for data.

posts.title: What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale?
posts.summary:
The path to widespread deployment of co-packaged optics depends on solving challenges in manufacturing, testing, and operations.
The post What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Co-packaged optics (CPO) is moving from proof-of-concept to production, initially targeting scale-out switch ASICs where copper bandwidth is insufficient.
The transition to using CPO in scale-up networks—connecting thousands of XPUs—remains the next major technical hurdle for the industry.
Widespread adoption depends on standardizing manufacturing, testing, and supply chain operations to ensure cost-effective, high-volume deployment.

posts.title: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
posts.summary: The police-tech giant Flock is announcing today that it will change officers’ access to its nationwide network of license plate readers, in an apparent effort to quell a growing backlash and win back contracts lost amid concerns about mass surveillance and police abuse. Several changes aim directly at a problem that has made recent headlines:…
bullets: Flock is implementing mandatory criminal case number requirements for all license plate reader searches to curb unauthorized use by law enforcement.
The company is scaling an automatic auditing system to flag suspicious search patterns, though it has not yet allowed independent verification of the tool's efficacy.
Despite these guardrails, critics note that the system lacks verification for case numbers, allowing officers to bypass safeguards with generic or nonsensical entries.
Flock is also encouraging agencies to reduce data retention periods from 30 days to seven days to mitigate public backlash regarding mass surveillance.

posts.title: BYD's flash charging Qin Max sedan goes on sale in China for under $15,000
posts.summary:
The BYD Qin Max is the flagship of the Qin family, available in EV and DM-i versions.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD launched the Qin Max sedan, available in both DM-i plug-in hybrid and EV versions, starting at 99,900 yuan ($14,720).
The EV variant features BYD's second-generation Blade Battery and flash charging technology, allowing a 10% to 97% charge in nine minutes.
The launch is a strategic effort to revitalize the Qin family, which has seen sales volume halve over the past year.
